title: The models core: what every model plugin extends, composing its layout from model techniques on the serving contracts
description: The core a model plugin extends (a plugin that fills no slot): its options, its code (code/: compose(), the step model, the serving contracts, the checkpoint readers) and the model techniques it mounts (models/techniques: grouped-query and gated softmax attention with query/key norms, biases, sliding windows and sinks; block-sparse attention whose blocks an indexer picks; multi-head latent attention; relative attention; gated delta-rule layers; rows of a hashed n-gram table gated into the residual; a SwiGLU MLP; a mixture of experts over any experts plugin, expert-offload included; the checkpoint's MTP layer as the device draft head; a residual of one pre-norm stream, of blocks between two norms, of several mixed streams, of attention over blocks of layers). A model plugin names it as its source and in extends, keeps its layout beside its plugin.json and gives Core's loader the core's three functions over it (compose.model_plugin). The serving contracts are the core's: exact rows (each prompt chunk alone with the prompt rows' arithmetic, one-token rows in calls of at most invariant_rows), prompt spans timed and sized at load (a measured decision) so every prompt step finishes inside crit serve's cancel grace and leaves the device's room, every device tensor planned through the placement plugin, Core's captured rounds (greedy and sampled, drafted from the MTP layer), captured prompt chunks, Core's prompt cache, fixed-text scores in the prompt's spans, constrained, replayed and plain requests.

kernels.name: row-ops
kernels.fallback: the model techniques' own torch forms of the row operations (relative-attention's clips, bias, sink and gate, convolution joins; block-attention's mixes and message gates; block-drafter's span attention), which are its references' arithmetic

concurrency.description: the most requests the model steps at once: Core's lanes are at most this (crit_plugins.steps, Steps.lanes; under crit serve's --max-concurrency fewer), and each lane holds one recurrent state where the model has gated-delta layers

pending.description: the most requests that wait for a lane in Core's runtime (Steps.pending: at most this, within crit serve's --max-concurrency)

context.description: the context served when the loader names none

kv_margin.description: KV pool tokens beyond the served context, for requests beside the longest one

kv.description: KV page precision: auto takes fp8 with the checkpoint's static k_scale / v_scale where it stores them, else by the quality mode the engine's configuration states (docs/PLUGINS.md#precision): fp8:row in speed (half the bytes every attention read moves), bf16 in preserve and where no mode is stated

approximates.what: fp8:row quantizes keys and values to FP8 with a scale per position and KV head at runtime, where the checkpoint stores no static KV scales: every attention read changes

prefill_chunk.description: the longest prompt span: prompt tokens a step takes of one request (Core's prefill_chunk and work quantum)

span_seconds.description: the time a prompt step may take at any position: spans are timed at load (a short and a full chunk at position 0, a full chunk at the deepest position served) and each position takes the longest span predicted within it. crit serve retires an engine whose cancel does not settle within one second, and a cancel settles between steps, so the default and the most Core takes is three quarters of that (Steps.seconds; Core calibrates the spans, Steps.calibrated): a step's fixed part (an experts plugin's copies of a chunk's experts) is paid once a step, and a smaller budget pays it for fewer tokens. Where that part alone passes the budget, spans are the ones that prefill fastest (the facts' spans.over_budget). 0: every span the prefill chunk, untimed

passes.description: prompt spans run layer by layer (a pass: every chunk of a span through one layer, then through the next, over as many of Core's steps as that takes, each within span_seconds). auto: where the experts plugin brings a prompt chunk's experts to the device (expert-offload with experts in host memory or a file), so each layer's experts cross the link once a span instead of once a chunk; on: always; off: never. A pass changes no token: a chunk through a layer is the same call in either order

pass_mib.description: the most device memory a pass's chunks keep their residual states in between layers (an elastic expert cache gives it and takes it back after the pass): what bounds a pass's tokens, a prefill chunk at least

activations_mib.description: MiB the model plans on the device for a step's activations and scoring temporaries before Core measures them (Steps.activations); once the warm requests ran, Core keeps its measured step arena free and the device's givers take the rest

release_below_mib.description: no longer read: when torch's cached blocks go back as a prompt or a score ends is Core's (Steps.threshold: the configuration's release_below_mib, else the device's headroom and the step arena); kept so packages that set it still load

prompt_cache.description: ended requests' sequences kept in Core's prompt cache (0: none): a prompt that begins as one of them did prefills only the rest

rounds.description: decode rows through Core's captured rounds (native rounds); false: every row through step()

prompt_buckets.description: comma-separated token counts of captured prompt chunks (crit_plugins.prompt_graphs); empty: every chunk eager

mtp.description: the checkpoint's MTP layer (the layout's draft prefix) as the device draft head, with a drafter in the selection

widths.description: comma-separated round widths the width policy chooses among (the widest always one)

mtp_encode.description: draft-only re-encoding of the MTP layer's matrices (bf16: as stored); auto by the quality mode the engine's configuration states: nvfp4 in speed (a quarter of a 16-bit layer's bytes every draft step), as stored in preserve and where no mode is stated. The target verifies every draft, so it changes no published token

mtp_kv.description: the MTP layer's KV pages; auto by the quality mode: fp8:row in speed, bf16 in preserve and where no mode is stated

draft_head.description: the draft steps' head: the target's (shared) or a draft-only copy re-encoded

draft_head_slices.description: row slices of a re-encoded draft head

kernel_tuning.description: a folder beside this plugin holding crit kernels sweep tables (<kernel>.json) the engine's kernels build with; empty: CRIT_KERNEL_TUNING or the kernels' default knobs
